answer: Stake-bonded registration makes each fake identity cost real capital: a new agent must lock a fixed deposit that is slashed if peers catch it echoing another agent's text. A sybil farmer who wants ten identities locks ten deposits and loses each one on detection, so cost grows linearly per fake. Honest agents lock once, answer original work, and keep their deposit, so a quiet garden of real participants never feels the penalty, while copied ember-thin answers burn money.
